trip.title: South Korea Trip — Seoul · Gyeongju · Busan
trip.note: Oct 31 – Nov 22, 2026 (22 nights). Autumn shoulder season — leaf-peeping, mild temps, lighter crowds than summer, and generally better hotel rates than spring high season. Prices below are typical nightly USD figures for a standard double; always confirm the live rate for YOUR dates on the hotel's official site.

split.recommended: Seoul 8 nights (Oct 31–Nov 8) · Gyeongju 6 nights (Nov 8–Nov 14) · Busan 8 nights (Nov 14–Nov 22)
split.rationale: Seoul is the biggest city and main transport hub, so bookending the trip there is practical. Gyeongju is compact (5–7 nights = relaxed pace + day trips to Bulguksa & Yangdong Village). Busan is large and spread across two personalities (Haeundae beachside vs. Nampo old town), so 7–9 nights lets you split between neighborhoods.
alternatives: More Seoul: 10 / 4 / 8 (Gyeongju trimmed to a long weekend)

arrivalNight.title: First night in Seoul — officially verified late-arrival shortlist
arrivalNight.requirement: For the first booked night only, use a hotel with a currently documented 24-hour reception/front desk. Official hotel or government-tourism evidence is preferred, and every option still requires a late-arrival message.
arrivalNight.definition: A current official hotel/brand page, government tourism listing, or major trusted booking platform must explicitly show 24-hour reception/front-desk coverage or an equivalent anytime check-in signal. This is not a guarantee that an unannounced no-show will be held: book the landing date, share the flight number, and obtain written confirmation for a possible after-midnight arrival.

decision.recommended: Book Somerset Palace Seoul — Studio Executive for the first night.
decision.why: It has the strongest source chain in the shortlist: the official Ascott property page lists 24-hour reception, the official room page lists one queen bed plus a private bathroom and washer/dryer, and the property is about three minutes from Anguk Station in the palace/Insadong area.
decision.airportFallback: Choose Grand Hyatt Incheon only if avoiding the late trip into Seoul matters more than waking up in the city. It is near ICN, not a Seoul sightseeing base.

steps.title: Reserve the actual arrival date
steps.body: A hotel night begins on the calendar date you land, even if you reach the property after midnight. Do not reserve the following night by mistake.

steps.title: Send a late-arrival note immediately
steps.body: Add your flight number, 21:00 scheduled ICN arrival, and a note that delays could put you past midnight. Ask the hotel to confirm the reservation will be held.

steps.title: Use a taxi if the final public-transport option is tight
steps.body: A 24-hour reception solves the check-in risk, not the airport-to-hotel transport risk. Check live rail/bus and shuttle schedules on the day; do not assume a hotel shuttle runs overnight.

steps.title: Keep the confirmation accessible
steps.body: Save the property address in Korean/English, the hotel phone number, and the booking confirmation before your flight.

candidates.label: Top pick — strongest official-source evidence
candidates.frontDesk: 24-hour reception listed by the official property site
candidates.room: Studio Executive — one queen bed, private bathroom, kitchen and washer/dryer
candidates.station: Anguk Station — about a 3-minute walk; Gwanghwamun/Jonggak about 5 minutes
candidates.estimatedRate: $140–190/night for Studio Executive — planning estimate, not a live quote
candidates.why: It keeps night one in central Seoul while pairing the clearest official 24-hour-reception statement with a queen room and useful in-room laundry for the longer stay.
candidates.tradeoff: It is in the palace/Insadong area rather than Myeongdong. The late airport-to-city journey still depends on live rail/bus timing.
candidates.bookingNote: Book Studio Executive for the calendar date you land, send the flight number, and ask Ascott to confirm the room will be held after midnight.
candidates.evidenceLabel: Official Somerset / Ascott property brochure: 24-hour reception, room facilities and normal hours
candidates.evidenceQuote: The official property data lists “24-hour reception”; its Studio Executive page lists one queen-size bed, a private bathroom, and a washing machine and dryer.

candidates.label: Central Myeongdong pick — trusted listing evidence
candidates.room: Deluxe Double — one queen bed (approx. 150 × 200 cm)
candidates.estimatedRate: $150–185/night — planning estimate, not a live quote
candidates.why: The simplest one-hotel start: the late-arrival requirement is covered without giving up a central base for the rest of Seoul.
candidates.tradeoff: The ICN-to-Myeongdong journey is still the variable after a delay. Switch to a taxi if the final train or bus connection is no longer comfortable.
candidates.bookingNote: Book the Deluxe Double specifically, then message the property with your flight number and possible after-midnight arrival.
candidates.evidenceLabel: Property listing: 24-hour front desk, en-suite bathroom, and Myeongdong Station proximity
candidates.evidenceQuote: The property listing states that L7 Myeongdong has a 24-hour front desk and is a few minutes' walk from Myeongdong Station.

candidates.label: Official-tourism value option — central Myeongdong
candidates.room: Standard Room with 1 Double Bed — private bathroom; exact bed width needs confirmation
candidates.station: Euljiro 1-ga — about 4 minutes; Myeongdong Station about 7 minutes
candidates.estimatedRate: $100–130/night — planning estimate, not a live quote
candidates.why: It provides a lower-cost central option with round-the-clock reception documented by the Korea Tourism Organization and direct official booking through Accor.
candidates.tradeoff: The cited room is a double, not a confirmed queen. Choose Somerset or L7 if bed width is non-negotiable.
candidates.bookingNote: Confirm the exact bed width, reserve the landing date on Accor, then message the hotel with the flight number and possible post-midnight arrival.
candidates.evidenceQuote: The government-run VISITKOREA property entry says that all rooms have standard business-hotel facilities and the hotel provides “a 24-hour reception service.”

candidates.label: Second Myeongdong value pick
candidates.estimatedRate: $120–138/night for the Deluxe — planning estimate, not a live quote
candidates.why: A more economical central option that still keeps the one-queen-bed and near-station preferences when you choose the Deluxe room.
candidates.tradeoff: The less-expensive Standard/Double rooms in the planner use a smaller double bed, so do not select those if the queen-size requirement is non-negotiable.
candidates.bookingNote: Choose the Deluxe room, not Standard Double; message the hotel with the late-arrival details after booking.
candidates.evidenceQuote: The property listing says the hotel has a 24-hour front desk that can assist with laundry, luggage storage, and ticketing.

candidates.label: Most delay-proof — sleep by ICN, move to Seoul tomorrow
candidates.location: Incheon Airport area — not central Seoul
candidates.frontDesk: Hotel is listed as open 00:00–23:59; current booking listing says check-in ends anytime
candidates.room: 1 King Bed — confirm the selected room and rate at booking
candidates.station: Airport-area hotel; plan its airport transfer directly rather than a Seoul subway connection
candidates.why: This removes the long late-night trip into central Seoul. It is the safest fallback if your priority is getting to bed quickly after a delayed flight.
candidates.tradeoff: You will need to transfer into Seoul the next morning, so this is intentionally only an arrival-night fallback.
candidates.bookingNote: Check the property's current airport-transfer timetable and notify it of your flight number; do not assume every hotel shuttle runs after midnight.
candidates.evidenceLabel: Official Hyatt property hours + major trusted booking listing with check-in end “anytime”
candidates.evidenceQuote: Hyatt’s official property data publishes daily opening hours from 00:00 to 23:59; Expedia lists check-in as ending anytime. Contact the hotel with the flight number and obtain a written acknowledgement.
candidates.evidenceType: Official hotel/brand + major trusted booking platform

arrivalNight.verificationStandard: Official hotel/brand source preferred; government tourism authority or major trusted booking platform accepted when the property site does not publish reception hours.
